90429.overview:
The player is in a room filled with blocks and a bunch of fierce spods whom the player must kill without being touched in order to advance to the next stage. Spods destroy blocks as they walk about. Blocks can be destroyed if pressed when against a wall or another block, but can also be pushed a distance, squashing spods. Spods can also be killed by pushing against an edge which will turn yellow for a few seconds. If the spod walks in that spot it becomes stunned, and the player can walk over the spod to kill it.

There are three star blocks on the level that can't be destroyed. These can destroy spods, but can also be knocked in a line for bonus points. On early stages there are four Spods to kill, but on higher stages this number increases. Only four spods can appear on a screen at a time. The player starts with three lives, and an extra life is awarded at 50,000 points.

90434.overview:
Nightshade was released for the BBC Micro in 1985 by Ultimate Play The Game. It was the first game using the Filmation II graphics engine.
The new engine allowed scrolling around a large world and arcade-like play, rather than the room-based puzzles of the earlier Filmation titles

The BBC version is quite a bit different from the other formats, firstly the game is totally monochrome, usually blue, secondly the ammunition bar is under the play screen instead of by the side of it, this is because the play area is considerably larger than any other port, it also plays faster, and has the annoying quirk of enemies materialising on top of the hero removed. There is no joystick control and no way to redefine the keys to the players liking.

91088.overview:
Night World is a 1-player arcade game featuring Lee Lance the explorer, who must find his way through the cavernous underworld collecting objects that will lead to the magical Golden Fleece and his final escape route.

Lee Lance can move laterally and jump, and travels between a number of rooms by jumping from platforms. A time counter on the bottom of the screen shows progression from day to night and, during the nighttime, Lee Lance turns into a gargoyle, allowing him to jump to higher platforms. The player has a health bar at the top of the screen that is drained by coming into physical contact with enemies or other dangers.

Though the Golden Fleece can not be collected in the game, the player's goal is to collect the four prisms and escape to the Inner Worl

116516.overview: Nifty Lifty is a simple arcade game. The player must collect various items such as hearts, small toy trains, tanks, umbrellas, and climb up while avoiding dangerous lifts going up and down. Each contact with a lift results in a loss of life. The character is controlled with two keys to move left and right. When the edge of the screen is reached, where the arrow is, the game automatically moves the character to the upper floor. A time bonus is provided for completing levels quickly.

122643.overview:
Nevryon is a fast sideways-scrolling shoot-'em-up.

The object is to fly your Cavern Fighter over and through various types of terrain, shooting alien vessels in formations and larger weapon structures on the ground, roof and in the air. At the same time, extra weapons like increased firepower become available and bonus pods appear on the screen to be picked up.
When the end of each level is reached, there is quite a large alien fortress to be destroyed. This is initially quite easy but gets progressively harder when more different alien weapons are present.

There are eight levels in the game which fit into four scenarios:
The Giant Battle Cruiser
The Asteroid Base
The Planet Surface/Caves
The Alien Beast
There are two levels for each, the second being harder than the first.

126343.overview:
You play a caveman who must knock food down to his family while fending off various creatures.

As well as the standalone release, Neanderthal Man was also released as part of Alligata's Chartbuster compilation which included Blagger, Eagle Empire, Monaco and Web Runner.

128844.overview:
Cyril the Squirrel is due to start hibernating but has yet to collect and store all the nuts he needs to get through the winter. You play as Cyril in this platform game where the screen scrolls in both left and right directions when you move. The game is spread over eight levels and you must collect all the nuts on each level to move to the next level within a time limit.
As you move and jump around each level, there are various creatures that include snails, beetles and butterflies that move from the right to the left either on the ground or on a erratic flight path in the air. If you touch any creature then you lose one of three lives and start at the beginning of the level having to collect all the nuts again. Before you start the game you can select the speed (slow or fast) and your starting level.

136344.overview:
The player, as Sleepy Joe, must make his way around the maze collecting the eight keys required to open the Dark Door of Deeper Sleep and progress to the next level, whilst avoiding the Springy Thingies which bounce around the maze. Occasionally a cup of black coffee will appear; touch it and the bouncing beasties will disappear for a short time allowing Joe to collect his keys unhindered.

Nightmare Maze was developed by Mike Williams of MRM. It was originally published for the BBC Micro by MRM, with a re-release for the BBC and Electron by Blue Ribbon.

136354.overview:
From the depths of space come Earth's deadliest adversaries: the Vogons. Destroy successive waves of these barbaric creatures as they hurtle towards you in convoys.
Each convoy consists of a number of Vogons which snake their way down from the top of the screen, changing direction if they hit an asteroid and splitting into two if hit in the middle.
As the game progresses, additional hazards are introduced. Chargers dive-bomb your shuttle craft and Crushers bounce across the ionosphere. The Crawlers create 'warp vectors' from asteroids in their path. If the Vogons come into contact with any of these they are immediately transported to the bottom of the screen.
Asteroids (including the warp vectors) can be destroyed by two shots, the second shot causing debris to fall towards your craft.
An extra life is awarded at 5,000 points.

153317.overview: A 3D version of the classic light cycles/tron game in which you navigate a grid and must avoid your own trail whilst forcing the computer to crash into something.

206682.overview: Full flight simulation was offered in this innovative early release. Landing at night, you must take off, climb, control the plane mid air, and then land successfully. As well as basic steering, rudders, flaps, wheels and airspeed come under your control. There are five different flight challenges featured, including navigation as well as flight skills, plus a rolling demo on startup. A full instrument panel is provided for each of these, allowing you to judge speeds and distances.

440585.overview: Fourth in Larsoft's text adventure series, The Nine Dancers has you play the part of a reporter who's been asked to write an article on the stories and the legents connected with some of the local tourist sites. Due to how the game was written, it was directly compatible on multiple platforms, namely BBC, Electron and Master 128.
